extracted.intended_audience: readers and students of George MacDonald's Alec Forbes; people needing help with Scots dialect in the novel
extracted.subtask_description: A compressed glossary of Scots words and phrases found in George MacDonald's Alec Forbes of Howglen, intended to help readers understand dialectal conversation and references in the novel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Glossary file format (CSV-ready compressed format)
rubrics_metrics.description: This list is a compressed format that consists of three columns for 'word', 'definition', and 'notes'. It is set up with a comma between each item and a hard return at the end of each definition so the section can be cut and pasted into its own text file and imported into a database or spreadsheet as a comma separated variable file (.csv).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you cannot import directly, perform a search-and-replace for commas in this section (the transcriber states they have not used any commas in words, definitions, or notes) and replace commas with spaces or tabs. The intent is to make the list machine-importable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intended scope and accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: The list was compiled by the transcriber from context, help from a local informant, and reference works; it was not meant to be a comprehensive Scots dialect dictionary but an aid to understanding conversations and references in this novel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The compiler aimed to be thorough but acknowledges possible mistakes and omissions and welcomes feedback. Treat definitions as a reading aid rather than an authoritative or exhaustive lexicon.
